story: Shiva lives in meditation on Mount Kailash with Parvati, their sons Ganesha and Kartikeya, and his bull Nandi. When the gods and asuras churned the ocean of milk, a deadly poison, halahala, rose first and threatened all creation. Shiva drank it and held it in his throat, which turned blue and gave him the name Neelakantha.
belief: Shaivas see Shiva as the supreme reality itself, beyond birth and death. He is worshipped above all as the lingam, and Maha Shivaratri is his great night of fasting and vigil.
turns: Not knowing who the boy guarding Parvati's door was, he cut off his head in anger. It was her son, and Shiva restored him with an elephant's head as Ganesha. When his first wife Sati died at her father Daksha's sacrifice, his grief-fuelled dance nearly destroyed the world.
facts: The 12 Jyotirlingas, including Kashi Vishwanath and Somnath, are among Hinduism's holiest pilgrimage sites.
As Nataraja, Lord of Dance, his cosmic dance stands for the cycle of creation and destruction.
The Ganga is said to flow down through his matted hair so that her fall does not shatter the earth.
